source_text:
Ὅρα, μή τίς σε πλανήσῃ ἀπὸ ταύτης τῆς ὁδοῦ τῆς διδαχῆς, ἐπεὶ παρεκτὸς θεοῦ σε διδάσκει.
εἰ μὲν γὰρ δύνασαι βαστάσαι ὅλον τὸν ζυγὸν τοῦ κυρίου, τέλειος ἔσῃ: εἰ δ’ οὐ δύνασαι, ὅ δύνῃ, τοῦτο ποίει.
περὶ δὲ τῆς βρώσεως, ὅ δύνασαι βάστασον: ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ εἰδωλοθύτου λίαν πρόσεχε λατρεία γάρ ἐστι θεῶν νεκρῶν.
thought_title: Guard the way of the teaching
orientation: The anonymous teacher is closing the Two Ways instruction and turning to practical rules, warning the hearer not to be led away from the way of the teaching.
pass_a_gloss: See [to it], lest anyone lead you astray from this way of the teaching, since apart from God he teaches you. For if indeed you are able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, you will be perfect; but if you are not able, what you are able [to do], this do. And concerning food, what you are able [to do], bear; but from the idol-sacrificed [meat] very much be on guard; for it is worship of dead gods.

choices.why: The imperative is a warning formula; 'see to it' preserves the force of the command without modernizing to 'watch out' in the literal pass.
The phrase means teaching that is outside or without God's authority; 'apart from God' keeps the spatial metaphor of the Greek.

choices.english: the whole yoke of the Lord
choices.why: The glossary fixes 'yoke' for ζυγός, and 'whole' preserves the adjective's force that the full set of obligations is in view.
rejected: the entire yoke of the Lord

choices.why: The Greek is a substantivized adjective meaning food offered to idols; supplying 'meat' makes the sense clear in English while keeping the literal term.

choices.english: for it is worship of dead gods
choices.why: The explanatory γάρ clause gives the reason for the warning; 'worship' is the standard sense of λατρεία and 'dead gods' keeps the genitive phrase literal.
rejected: for it is service to dead gods
for it is the worship of dead gods

pass_b_english: See to it that no one leads you astray from this way of teaching, because such a person teaches you apart from God.
If you are able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, you will be perfect; but if you are not able, do what you can.
Concerning food, bear what you can. But be strictly on guard against meat sacrificed to idols, for it is worship of dead gods.

last_rejected.quote: because such a person teaches you apart from God
last_rejected.why: παρεκτὸς means 'without/apart from' but the sense is 'teaches you without God [being involved]', not 'apart from God' as a location.
last_rejected.fix: for whoever teaches you does so without God
last_rejected.ruling: παρεκτὸς θεοῦ means 'apart from God'; 'teaches you apart from God' correctly conveys without God's involvement.
